test_title: SSC CPO 2025 Official Paper (Held On 12 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Vichitrachitta, Chitrakarapuli, and Chaityakari are the titles given to which of the following rulers?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahendravarman I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Mahendravarman I** was a ruler of the Pallava dynasty in South India, reigning from approximately **600 CE to 630 CE**. He was a significant patron of arts and architecture.
 
• He was bestowed with titles such as **Vichitrachitta** (curious-minded), **Chitrakarapuli** (tiger among artists), and **Chaityakari** (temple builder) due to his contributions to temple architecture and his innovative mind.
 
• Mahendravarman I introduced the **rock-cut architecture** style in South India, which marked the beginning of the Dravidian style of temple construction. His creations are evident in places like **Mahabalipuram**.
 
• Under his reign, the Pallava dynasty saw significant developments in **art, literature, and culture**. He was also a playwright and musician, authoring works like **Mattavilasa Prahasana**, a Sanskrit play.
 
• Mahendravarman I was initially a Jain but later converted to **Shaivism**, which influenced his temple-building activities dedicated to Lord Shiva.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mahendravarman I's Contributions:**

 
 
• He is credited with constructing some of the earliest examples of **rock-cut temples** in South India, such as the **Mandagapattu temple** in Tamil Nadu, which is dedicated to the Hindu trinity (Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva).
 
• The temples built during his period reflect a transition from wooden structures to **stone architecture**, showcasing durability and artistic intricacies.
 
 
 
• **Other Titles of Mahendravarman I:**
 
 
• Vichitrachitta (curious-minded): Reflects his intellectual curiosity and innovation in art and architecture.
 
• Chitrakarapuli (tiger among artists): Highlights his exceptional artistic abilities and patronage of art.
 
• Chaityakari (temple builder): Points to his pioneering contributions to temple construction.
 
 
 
• **Pallava Dynasty:**
 
 
• The Pallavas ruled parts of South India between the **3rd and 9th centuries CE**.
 
• They are renowned for their contributions to **Dravidian architecture**, particularly in Mahabalipuram and Kanchipuram.
 
 
 
• **Other Rulers in the Options:**
 
 
• **Kirtivarman I:** A ruler of the Chalukya dynasty; he is not associated with the titles mentioned in the question.
 
• **Narasimhavarman II:** A Pallava king known for his architectural contributions but not associated with the specific titles mentioned.
 
• **Parantaka I:** A Chola king known for his military conquests and temple-building activities but not linked to the given titles.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mattavilasa Prahasana:** This satirical play written by Mahendravarman I mocks religious hypocrisy and the confusion among religious sects of his time.
 
• **Conversion to Shaivism:** His conversion from Jainism to Shaivism had a significant impact on his patronage of Shaivite temples and art.
 
• **Legacy:** Mahendravarman I's architectural innovations laid the groundwork for later Pallava kings, such as Narasimhavarman I, who further expanded the temple-building tradition.
